answer: A bonded reputation ledger works like a river feeding a lagoon: new agents start in shallow water with tiny limits, and only sustained honest work deepens their channel. Each agent periodically publishes a verifiable beacon attesting to completed tasks, and peers check it against on-chain history. Creating thousands of fake identities gains nothing, because each fake must separately pay the stake, wait through the slow trust ramp, and risk slashing if its beacon is false, so Sybil scale becomes expensive, slow, and easy to spot.
